prompt: Task: precise subject-only identity replacement inside the supplied mask, not image redesign and not general style transfer. Image 1 is the immutable edit target and the sole authority for the complete canvas: crop, subject scale and placement, seated pose, body angle, head tilt, upward gaze, gentle sweet expression, orange-yellow-teal background, every background paint mark, palette, saturation, contrast, lighting, edge rhythm and overall finish. Preserve all of it exactly except the animal's species and identity. Image 2 is the absolute authority for how every part of the replacement face and fur must be designed and painted. Copy its appealing facial relationships: gentle head tilt, coordinated upward gaze, balanced soft rounded-almond eyes, relaxed upper eyelids, full soft cheeks, broad rounded muzzle, small rounded nose, short philtrum and subtle closed-mouth smile with gently raised corners. Copy its broad confident dry-brush marks, clean layered colour shapes and sparse broken edges. The new cat's face, eyes, nose, mouth, ears and whisker area must use this same painted language. The face must not read as a photograph placed inside a painting. Image 3 is a deliberately non-photographic identity structure guide already aligned to Image 2's expression. Use it only for mature feline head and body anatomy, Dragon Li ear identity, natural adult proportions, brown tabby colours and recognisable stripe placement. Image 2 remains authoritative if any facial feature conflicts. Do not copy Image 3's plain background or framing, and do not infer or restore photographic detail that is absent from Image 3. Replace the original white dog with exactly one adult Dragon Li tabby cat while transferring Image 1's exact pose, head angle, gaze, expression, silhouette occupancy and body gesture onto the cat. Adapt only the anatomy necessary to read as an adult cat. Preserve mature proportions; do not make a kitten and do not enlarge the head, eyes or cheeks. Style and appealing expression win over literal identity microdetail whenever they conflict. Represent tabby markings as broad painterly strokes, never individual fur strands. Use only a few short painted whisker suggestions, never photographic whiskers. Both eyes must be similar in size, softly rounded-almond rather than circular, aimed at the same upward point, with relaxed lids and only one small clean highlight each. No black button eyes, no wide-eyed surprise, no hollow dark eye mask, no pinched triangular muzzle, no long vertical philtrum, no rigid W-shaped mouth, no downturned mouth corners and no exaggerated vertical ears. Preserve adult identity through the mature body and natural feline structure, not through a severe or angular face. The cheeks and muzzle may remain soft and friendly without turning the cat into a kitten. No realistic iris texture, reflective eyeball, wet nose, detailed hair follicles, fine fur direction, photographic facial anatomy, 3D volume rendering, smooth airbrushing or pasted mixed-media face. Change no background, scene, composition, subject placement, palette, saturation or brushwork. Remove only the platform watermark and account ID already covered by the mask. No new text, objects, accessories, extra animal or anatomy changes.
